_doc.what: Annotated sample for .bee/config.json — copy the sections you need; every key here is optional (missing keys fall back to safe defaults). JSON has no comments, so this _doc block is the documentation; bee ignores unknown top-level keys, but remove _doc from your real config to keep it lean.
_doc.hooks: Per-hook kill switches. All nine ship enabled; set one to false only to debug that hook. Names match the hook files: session-init, prompt-context, write-guard, model-guard, state-sync, chain-nudge, session-close, tools-logger, codex-subagent-audit.
_doc.guards: idle_gate=true blocks source edits when no bee work is active (phase idle / compounding-complete). Disable per-repo only if you accept unrouted edits: bee config set --key guards.idle_gate --value false. max_read_lines (default 800) caps how many lines a single inbound file read may pull before the read guard trims it.
_doc.commands: The host project's own lifecycle commands — record real runnable commands, not descriptions. The keys are setup, start and test. `test` is the ONE declared test command. Tests prove at the boundary: the green base check, `bee close`, `bee worktree merge`, and CI all run it; a cap is commit-only proof and records `tests: boundary`. `commands.verify` was retired in 2.1.0 — a leftover one is ignored and onboarding warns on it; delete it and move its command to `test`. A project that deliberately runs no tests sets `test` to the exact sentinel string `"none"` instead of a real command — every gate above then reports itself disabled in one loud line rather than running (decision 55b951e1). Per-language recipes (node/go/rust/python/php): docs/config-reference.md.

gate_bypass.values: false | "normal" | "full" | "total" (legacy true = normal). Set via the bee-bypass-gate skill, not by hand.
gate_bypass.false: default — every gate stops for the human.
gate_bypass.normal: auto-approves Gates 1-2 for tiny/small/standard work; high-risk/hard-gate work, secret reads, and review-P1 still stop.
gate_bypass.full: also auto-approves high-risk/hard-gate Gates 1-2; only secret reads and a review P1 still stop.
gate_bypass.total: zero stops: every gate, secret reads, and review P1 findings auto-proceed. The loud session banner reminds you it is on.

models.what: Only the CHEAPER tiers are configured, keyed by runtime (claude | codex) then slot (extraction | generation | review | advisor). The ceiling is never configured — it is always the session model. A missing/null slot = prompt-budget tier (the marker alone carries the tier; the subagent inherits the session model).

slot_shapes.string: "haiku" — plain model name; dispatches carry it as the model param (economics: effective_model_status=pinned on claude).
slot_shapes.object_cli: { "kind": "cli", "command": "...", "promptVia": "stdin" } — external CLI executor. GATHER-ONLY by design: cell execution against a cli-shaped slot is refused (cli_tier_gather_only); gathers/reviewers/advisors run through it with the prompt piped via stdin. See config-sample-cli-executors.json for full examples.
slot_shapes.null: slot unset — prompt-budget tier; on codex-native transport the effective model is inherited-or-unknown (the dispatch log records the honest split).

models.advisor: The AO3/AO13 consult identity required before Gate 2's execution component opens on high-risk work. Claude default: fable (the session-class model). Set null to skip the advisor line in worker prompts when no advisor resolves.
models.codex_note: On codex-cli 0.144.4 native subagents cannot pin a per-agent model — a string here records the REQUESTED model; the dispatch log will still say effective_model_status=inherited-or-unknown until a capability probe proves per-agent selection.

_doc.dogfood_repos: Only used in bee's own source repo (self-improvement loops); host projects can omit or leave [].
_doc.product_root: Optional, for the workshop+nested-product topology only: where the product's own docs live when they are NOT beside .bee/ (path relative to the bee root, or absolute). Unset = the bee root; do not set it speculatively — a set-but-missing path warns loudly on every read.
_doc.cells_archive_on_close: true (default) lets a green `bee close` retire the feature's capped cells into .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/, out of the path status/orient parse on every call. Set false only if your own tooling reads .bee/cells/*.json by path; reverse with bee cells unarchive --feature <f>.
_doc.ship_visibility: How finished work is surfaced: "off" (default) or "draft-pr". An unrecognized value normalizes to "off" and says so once, by name.
_doc.worktree_first: Code-touching feature work lives in its own worktree; the write guard refuses feature edits made in the main checkout. Set to the exact string "off" to disable that refusal for a repo that deliberately works in main.
_doc.worktree_cleanup_on_merge: true (default) lets `bee worktree merge` remove the worktree directory, delete its branch, and drop its grant automatically on a merge that merged something (opt one merge out with --no-cleanup). Set false to opt the whole repo out; a non-boolean value here is refused, never silently read as either outcome.
_doc.uat_before_merge: true (default, i.e. absent) makes `bee worktree merge` enforce the `uat` gate for standard/high-risk features. Set false to turn the door off repo-wide; a non-boolean value here refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID rather than guessing.
_doc.staging_before_merge: true (default, i.e. absent) keeps the staging mixing ground in use. Set false to make `bee staging add`/`bee staging rebuild` refuse STAGING_DISABLED, so the repo runs feature worktree -> uat gate -> main with no staging step; a non-boolean value here refuses STAGING_CONFIG_INVALID. Independent of uat_before_merge — the uat gate itself is unaffected.
_doc.doc_viewer: Opt-in URL prefix for a local doc viewer (e.g. mdview). base_url + project join as <base_url>/p/<project>/<repo-relative-path>, injected into the session preamble and the compaction capsule so agent prose links docs as URLs instead of bare paths. Unset = today's bare paths, silently. A half-set key (one field missing or empty, or a wrong-shaped value) produces no URL plus one stderr line naming the key. bee joins the URL, it does not encode it — a path containing a space needs percent-escaping by whoever writes the link.
